doc.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995

title: Learning jazz from string bands and blues changes
summary: He learned from visiting string musicians; jazz is attack on notes and adding passing chords to a twelve-bar blues.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: No, well from other string band musicians coming through there and they’re playing different tunes and as far as jazz, I mean jazz is just the way you attack some notes, you know, from like an eighth note to a sixteenth note or something. And you go from just playing a tune with knowing the chords and things, that helps you to add something to the tune. And you know, the easiest thing, like a blues, you know a blues is a twelve measure thing, and actually, you can actually take four chords and play the whole twelve measures you know. And then you can add fifteen or twenty more chords to it, you know, passing chords.
